hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Layered extension-host core + a thin terminal-styled webview (alternative a1). Per-provider stream adapter normalizes each CLI's native structured stream into one sc2 event union; extension observes, never orchestrates (k8).

boundary.internal: Subprocess spawn mechanics, per-provider native-stream parsing, the exact claude/codex flags (stream/resume spike), backpressure/cancellation, and error normalization stay private to S002; consumers see only sc2 TurnEvent + sc5 StreamAdapter/ProviderRegistry.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A — foundational contracts (design system + CLI bridge)

api.name: StreamAdapter.run

parameters.name: req
parameters.purpose: The turn to execute: provider, prompt, optional resume SessionHandle, and cwd (the workspace path scoping the CLI).

returns.meaning: A lazily-produced stream of normalized sc2 TurnEvents; the consumer for-awaits it (natural backpressure). Completes after a terminal 'done' (or 'error') event.

errors.condition: The CLI cannot be spawned, exits non-zero, or emits an unparseable/native-protocol-violating line — surfaced as a terminal error event, never a thrown reject.

preconditions: req.provider is a member of ProviderRegistry.available
The provider CLI binary is installed and authenticated via its own OAuth session (k2)
postconditions: No direct cloud REST call is made by the extension (k2)
Execution is a directly-spawned subprocess, not routed through the daemon (k1)
Every yielded item is a valid sc2 TurnEvent; no native provider-specific shape escapes the adapter

api.name: StreamAdapter.cancel

parameters.name: turnId
parameters.purpose: The id of the in-flight turn to abort (matches TurnEvent.turnId).

returns.meaning: Requests cancellation of the identified turn's subprocess; the run() iterable terminates (terminal done/error) promptly.

errors.condition: turnId is unknown or already finished — cancel is idempotent.

postconditions: The turn's subprocess is signalled to terminate; no orphaned process is left running

api.name: ProviderRegistry.get

parameters.name: id
parameters.purpose: Which agentic CLI adapter to retrieve ('claude' | 'codex').

returns.meaning: The per-provider adapter that spawns and normalizes that CLI's stream.

errors.condition: id is not one of the registered providers (should not occur when callers gate on `available`).

postconditions: Returns a StreamAdapter whose capabilities reflect that provider's spike-verified stream/resume support

api.name: ProviderRegistry.available

returns.meaning: The agentic CLIs actually installed/usable on this machine (claude and/or codex) — the source of truth the provider selector (S005) reads. Ollama is never a member (k4).

postconditions: Contains only agentic coding CLIs (claude/codex); never a plain-completion provider (k4)

errorCases.scenario: The selected provider CLI binary is not installed / not on PATH.
errorCases.detection: The subprocess spawn fails with ENOENT (spawn error event) before any stream line arrives.
errorCases.response: run() yields a single terminal error TurnEvent ('claude/codex CLI not found — install it or check PATH') and completes; ProviderRegistry omits that provider from `available`.
errorCases.userImpact: The turn fails immediately with a clear message; other installed providers keep working.

errorCases.scenario: The CLI process exits non-zero mid-turn.
errorCases.detection: The subprocess 'close' event fires with a non-zero exit code before a native terminal/done event was seen.
errorCases.response: Emit a terminal error TurnEvent with a trimmed stderr tail, then complete; partial assistant text stays rendered.
errorCases.userImpact: The user sees partial output plus a clear error line; they can retry.

errorCases.scenario: The CLI emits a line that is not valid structured output.
errorCases.detection: The per-provider parser's JSON.parse throws, or the parsed object matches no known native-event case.
errorCases.response: A non-fatal malformed line is logged (getLogger) and skipped — never yielded as a malformed TurnEvent; a wholly unintelligible stream yields one terminal error TurnEvent. The sc2 invariant (only valid events escape) holds.
errorCases.userImpact: Provider noise is invisible; a broken stream surfaces as one clear error, not corrupt UI.

errorCases.scenario: The CLI reports an authentication/authorization failure.
errorCases.detection: The provider emits its native auth-error event or exits with its documented auth exit code, matched in the mapper.
errorCases.response: Emit a terminal error TurnEvent telling the user to re-authenticate their CLI session; NO REST fallback, no stored credentials (k2).
errorCases.userImpact: Clear 'log in to your CLI' guidance; the extension never silently reaches a cloud endpoint.

errorCases.scenario: cancel(turnId) is called while a turn is streaming.
errorCases.detection: cancel() looks up the live subprocess handle for turnId (tracked internally).
errorCases.response: The subprocess is signalled to terminate; the iterable completes with terminal done (ok:false); no orphan remains. Unknown/finished id is a no-op.
errorCases.userImpact: Stopping a turn is immediate and clean.

edgeCases.input: req.resume provided but the provider's capabilities.resume is false.
edgeCases.expected: The adapter starts a fresh native session (ignores the resume handle) rather than erroring.
The adapter still spawns the turn and lets the CLI decide; it does not reject — passthrough (k8).

edgeCases.input: The CLI emits further native events after a terminal 'done'.
edgeCases.expected: Ignored; 'done' is terminal and the iterable has completed.

edgeCases.input: A burst of very high-frequency assistant-delta lines.
edgeCases.expected: Yielded as they arrive; for-await backpressure paces consumption (no whole-turn buffering).

edgeCases.input: No agentic CLI installed at all.
edgeCases.expected: available is empty; S005 shows 'no provider available'; get() is never called with an absent id.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Cloud LLM access happens ONLY through the user's installed claude/codex CLI OAuth session — no direct cloud REST, no stored credentials (k2). The daemon's CliProvider (src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts) is the in-repo precedent.
Chat CLI execution is a directly-spawned subprocess in the extension host, NOT routed through the daemon (k1).
The chat provider set is the agentic coding CLIs (claude/codex) only; ProviderRegistry never exposes a plain-completion provider (k4).
Only valid sc2 TurnEvents escape the adapter — no native provider-specific shape leaks to consumers.

alternativesConsidered.name: HLD contract as-is: AsyncIterable<TurnEvent> discriminated union
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Implement sc2/sc5 exactly as the HLD sketch — run() returns an AsyncIterable of the TurnEvent union, per-provider native→TurnEvent mappers private to the adapter.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep the HLD sc2 union + sc5 StreamAdapter/ProviderRegistry verbatim. run(req) is an async generator that spawns the provider CLI, reads its native structured stream line-by-line, yields normalized TurnEvents; cancel() kills the subprocess; capabilities.resume reflects native resume. Consumers for-await for natural backpressure; nothing provider-specific escapes.
pros: Zero contract drift from the approved HLD.
AsyncIterable gives natural backpressure + trivial async-generator fakes for tests.
cancel()+capabilities.resume already model the spike's provider-variable behaviours.
cons: More upfront structure than a monolith.
UnifiedDiff assumes the CLI stream exposes enough to build a diff; if a provider only reports post-content the adapter must compute it.

alternativesConsidered.name: Enveloped events: TurnEvent wrapped with monotonic seq + timestamp
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same union but each yielded item is wrapped in an envelope { seq, ts, event }.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Adopt the a1 union but yield an envelope carrying a per-turn monotonic seq + timestamp around each TurnEvent; AsyncIterable/StreamAdapter otherwise identical.
pros: Explicit seq makes ordering/replay assertions deterministic.
cons: Changes the approved sc2 contract — requires an HLD amendment + re-touch of every consumer.
Unwrap boilerplate for a benefit yield-order already provides in-scope.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Drops to partial on sc2: the seq/ts envelope changes the approved contract for an ordinal benefit that yield-order already provides in-scope, forcing an amendment for no in-scope gain. (The seq idea can live as an internal per-turn counter without changing sc2.)

alternativesConsidered.name: Pre/post content on file-edit instead of a UnifiedDiff
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: file-edit carries {path, before, after} full contents; S006 computes the diff.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same AsyncIterable<TurnEvent> but the file-edit variant carries before/after file contents instead of a UnifiedDiff; diff computation moves to the S006 renderer.
pros: Adapter stays dumber — no diff algorithm in S002.
cons: Changes the published sc2 file-edit shape — needs an amendment + re-touching S006.
Full before/after blobs per edit strain the streaming-throughput target.
Pushes diff computation to the renderer, weakening testable-host-logic.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Partial on sc2 (file-edit shape change) and strains the HLD streaming-throughput non-functional target by shipping full file blobs; worse than a1 with no compensating in-scope benefit.

citations.quotedText: sc2 TurnEvent union + sc5 StreamAdapter/ProviderRegistry owned by S002; extension-managed CLI spawn (k1), no REST/own CLI (k2), claude/codex only (k4), passthrough (k8), per-provider adapter quarantines the stream/resume spike.
Factory+deps-injection idiom (createWebviewPanelHost(deps)); vscode-free host modules; tests *.test; no existing chat/CLI-bridge — S002 net-new.
The daemon's CliProvider wraps claude+codex as structured-output-aware subprocesses — in-repo prior art for how these CLIs are invoked (reference for the S002 extension-side adapter + spike).
Cloud LLM access only via the claude/codex CLI binaries; no direct cloud REST. Daemon owns DB; IDE via IPC — but chat execution is deliberately extension-managed (k1).
The TurnEvent union + UnifiedDiff (sc2) and StreamAdapter/ProviderRegistry/TurnRequest/SessionHandle (sc5) type sketches implemented verbatim by S002.
